difficultyRationale: Requires reasoning about reordering and partially-constructed objects, not just naming the pattern — the classic double-checked-locking bug that the JSR-133 expert group had to formally document.
explanation: The inner synchronized block only protects the write to `helper` and the check inside it; the first, outer check at `if (helper == null)` happens outside any lock. Without `volatile`, the write to `helper` inside the constructing thread can become visible to another thread before that other thread also sees the writes the `Helper` constructor performed — the JMM does not forbid this reordering for a plain field. A thread hitting the fast outer path can therefore read a non-null `helper` that points at a `Helper` object still mid-construction.

options.text: There is no risk at all: the inner `synchronized` block fully synchronizes every read and write of `helper`, including the very first, unsynchronized check performed outside it by any thread, because the JVM extends every monitor's mutual-exclusion guarantee automatically to cover any field access anywhere in the enclosing class.
options.explanation: The outer `if (helper == null)` check is deliberately outside the synchronized block — that is the whole point of the "double-checked" optimization, to skip locking once `helper` is set. Because that check is unsynchronized, it is not covered by the monitor's happens-before guarantee at all.

options.text: A thread may call `getHelper()` concurrently and allocate two separate `Helper` instances, silently leaking one.
options.explanation: The inner check and assignment are inside the `synchronized (Helper.class)` block, so only one thread at a time can pass the inner `if` and construct a `Helper`; double allocation is exactly what the inner check prevents. The real risk here is about visibility, not duplicate construction.

options.text: A thread reading `helper` outside the lock, in the outer check, may see a reference to a `Helper` object whose constructor has not finished running, because the write to `helper` can become visible before the writes performed inside the constructor.
options.explanation: Correct, and this is exactly what the JSR-133 expert group's declaration on double-checked locking documents: without `volatile` (or an equivalent happens-before edge), a thread that takes the fast outer path can observe a non-null, partially constructed `Helper`.

options.text: The pattern throws `IllegalMonitorStateException` under high contention on JVMs that do not support biased locking.
options.explanation: `IllegalMonitorStateException` is thrown when code tries to unlock a monitor it doesn't hold, which has nothing to do with this pattern or with biased locking, an unrelated JIT optimization for uncontended locks.

references.title: "Double-Checked Locking is Broken" Declaration (JSR-133 expert group)
